quotes.text: SharePoint is not a basement. It is an evidence vault. But when you treat it like a shared drive, it acts like a mirror. It reflects your disorder back at you at scale.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Vivid framing of why SharePoint used as a file share multiplies chaos.

quotes.text: Dynamics is the system of events. Not the system of evidence. It was never meant to be a vault for files. It was meant to point, to bind, to link the narrative to artifact stored in a place designed for them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines the division of roles between Dynamics 365 and SharePoint.

quotes.text: People ask for search to do the remembering. Search is a lantern, not a ledger. It will show you what exists. It will not create a chain of custody.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why better search cannot replace structured document management.

quotes.text: Contracts do not start their seven years when someone uploads a draft to working. They start when the contract becomes law.

quotes.text: Do not create a label per team. Create a label per risk. Two or three confidential variants cover most of the city.

chapters.title: Case evidence and chain of custody
Purview as law: labels, retention, DLP

takeaways: Dynamics 365 should hold the events and SharePoint the evidence, linked through a document location created by rule for each record instead of attachments and copies.
Content types and required metadata such as lifecycle state, sensitivity and retention category give documents identity, so the approved version can always be found and proven.
Purview sensitivity labels, event-based retention and DLP enforce rights and endings automatically, and Copilot becomes a reliable witness only once this structure exists.
hook: Contracts get lost, versions get overwritten and audits fail because documents live in folders, inboxes and private channels instead of next to the records they prove. This episode is for Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 architects, admins and compliance owners who want a document management design that holds. You learn how to bind Dynamics records to governed SharePoint libraries with content types, Purview labels, event-based retention, DLP and Copilot.
